input.prompt:
## Objective

Find the exact release date of PostgreSQL 16 and its most significant performance improvement.

## Context

PostgreSQL 16 is a major version release of the PostgreSQL database. The research needs to identify: (1) the exact date it was released, and (2) the single most impactful performance improvement shipped in this version. Use web search and web fetch to locate official PostgreSQL release notes and credible technical sources.

## Output contract

Return ONLY the following, with no preamble or commentary:

### FINDINGS

1. PostgreSQL 16 release date:
   - Date: [exact date]
   - Source: [URL confirming the date]

2. Principal melhoria de performance:
   - Improvement: [description of the single most significant performance improvement]
   - Why it matters: [1-2 sentences on impact]
   - Source: [URL confirming this]

### SOURCES

- [label]: [URL]

## Boundaries

- Do NOT write any code.
- Do NOT include intermediate research steps or reasoning.
- If conflicting dates exist across sources, report both and flag the conflict.
- Every claim must have at least one source URL.
- Return only the formatted result, nothing else.

<task id="ses_02dc07af4ffe5Qf7SRu1Wti6aI" state="completed">
<task_result>
### FINDINGS

1. PostgreSQL 16 release date:
   - Date: **2023-09-14**
   - Source: PostgreSQL official release announcement [1], confirmed verbatim in release notes [2]

2. Principal melhoria de performance:
   - Improvement: **CPU acceleration via SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) on both x86 (SSE2) and ARM (NEON) architectures**, accelerating ASCII string detection, JSON string parsing, array operations, and subtransaction searches at the hardware level.
   - Why it matters: This is a cross-cutting, architectural change that benefits multiple subsystems simultaneously — COPY FROM bulk loads, JSON processing, C array searches, and transaction ID lookups all receive hardware-level throughput gains without application changes. The official release notes also document COPY improvements of up to 300% in some cases as a downstream beneficiary.
   - Source: PostgreSQL 16 official release announcement [1], release notes §E.15.3.1.2 "General Performance" [2]

### SOURCES

- [1] PostgreSQL 16 Release Announcement: https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-16-released-2715/ (2023-09-14)
- [2] PostgreSQL 16 Release Notes: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/release-16.html (2023-09-14)
</task_result>
</task>
